records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
records.summary: Article 5 of the Law on the People's Bank of China requires the PBOC to submit its decisions on the annual money supply, interest rates, exchange rates and other important matters specified by the State Council to the State Council for approval, and to implement those decisions; other monetary policy decisions are only filed with the State Council for record. Article 2 places the PBOC's formulation and implementation of monetary policy 'under the leadership of the State Council'.
records.detail: Read in the unofficial English translation published by the People's Bank of China itself (PDF on pbc.gov.cn, 167,418 bytes, extracted in full). The text's own heading states the Law was adopted at the Third Session of the Eighth National People's Congress on 18 March 1995 and revised by decision of the Standing Committee of the Tenth National People's Congress at its 6th Meeting on 27 December 2003; the date given here is the adoption date on the page, and the wording read is the 2003 revision. Article 53 provides that the Law takes effect on the date of promulgation; no repeal is stated. This is the standing arrangement rather than an episode, and it is distinct from the prosecution record the map already holds for China.
records.quote: The People's Bank of China shall submit to the State Council for approval its decisions concerning the annual money supply, interest rates, exchange rates
records.source_title: Law of the People's Republic of China on the People's Bank of China (unofficial translation, People's Bank of China)

records.summary: Under an institutional reform plan published in March 2023 by the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council, part of the People's Bank of China's duties were moved to a new National Financial Regulatory Administration, namely the supervision of financial holding companies and other financial groups and the protection of consumers of financial products; the plan also abolishes the central bank's county-level sub-branches.
records.detail: Source is the Chinese government's own English-language policy page (english.www.gov.cn), which names the two transferred functions in those words and describes the abolition of the central bank's county-level sub-branches. The page states only that the plan was published 'in March' and gives no formal plan name or exact day; the page itself is dated 17 April 2023, so the date field here is the month the page states, not a day. The page records no objection by the PBOC, and no consent by it either; it is filed as a state decision removing functions and money-handling structures from the bank. Distinct from the Fan Yifei prosecution record the map already holds.
records.source_title: Reform plan to see new financial regulatory body (State Council of the People's Republic of China, english.www.gov.cn policy watch)

records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
records.summary: Section 11 of the Reserve Bank Act 1959, headed 'Differences of opinion with Government on questions of policy', provides that where the Government and the relevant Board cannot agree on whether a policy is directed to the greatest advantage of the people of Australia, the Treasurer may recommend to the Governor-General, who may by order determine the policy to be adopted by the Bank, and the Board must give effect to that policy.
records.detail: Read on legislation.gov.au in the compilation of the Reserve Bank Act 1959 dated 1 March 2025, compilation No. 32 (the compilation date and number are printed on the document read). Subsection (3) requires the Board to give the Treasurer a statement of the disagreement; subsection (5) has the Government accept responsibility for the Bank adopting the policy; subsection (7) requires the Treasurer to table the order, a Government statement and the Board's statement in each House of Parliament within 15 sitting days. Still in force: the Act's current-compilation page on legislation.gov.au shows the Act as 'In force' with section 11 present and unrepealed in the table of provisions (that page reported compilation C2026C00375). The year in the date field is the year of the principal Act, which is the Act's own short title; the wording read is the 2025 compilation, which refers to 'the relevant Board'. Distinct from the 2023 public-pressure record the map already holds for Australia.
records.source_title: Reserve Bank Act 1959, compilation No. 32 (1 March 2025), s 11 (Federal Register of Legislation)

records.summary: Republic Act No. 11954, the Maharlika Investment Fund Act of 2023, requires that for the first and second fiscal years after it takes effect one hundred per cent of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas's total declared dividends be remitted to the National Government to capitalise the Maharlika Investment Corporation, up to the National Government's P50,000,000,000.00 initial subscription, and expressly amends section 2 of the BSP's charter to the extent needed to implement the Act.
records.detail: Text read at lawphil.net, which reproduces the Act as approved; sections 6(1)(a) and 51(a) carry the BSP dividend provision in identical words and section 57(a) states that section 2 of Republic Act No. 7653 as amended by Republic Act No. 11211 is expressly amended to the extent of ensuring full implementation of the Act. The same sections provide that the Monetary Board may recommend to the President a reduction in the BSP's contribution whenever economic conditions may warrant. The date is the approval date stated on the text, 18 July 2023; section 58 makes the Act effective on publication rather than approval, so the two-year diversion runs from publication. This records a statute diverting the central bank's dividends, which the BSP's charter otherwise applies to building up its own capital; the then governor publicly said the BSP could absorb the loss, so the record asserts no objection by the bank. Distinct from the 2016 public-pressure record the map holds for the Philippines. Filed on a law-library reproduction rather than the Official Gazette: the Senate issuances-library PDF path returned a 4,548-byte HTML page, not the Act.
records.quote: One hundred percent (100%) of the BSP's total declared dividends, as computed under Republic Act No. 7653
records.source_title: Republic Act No. 11954, Maharlika Investment Fund Act of 2023 (lawphil.net)

records.summary: In Opinion CON/2016/33 of 15 June 2016, requested by Croatia's Ministry of Finance, the European Central Bank found that draft amendments to the Law on Hrvatska Narodna Banka letting the State Audit Office audit the central bank's operations, and letting the Croatian Parliament discuss and vote on its annual report, were not in line with the principle of central bank independence in Article 130 of the Treaty and Article 7 of the Statute of the ESCB.
records.detail: Read in the opinion PDF hosted on the Croatian National Bank's own site. The ECB reasoned that the State Audit Office would be empowered to assess whether the bank meets its general objectives, including price stability, and that a parliamentary vote on the annual report could affect the bank's institutional independence because rights of third parties to approve, suspend, annul or defer a national central bank's decisions are incompatible with the Treaty. The draft also proposed capping the Governor's and Council members' terms at two; the ECB said current members should be allowed to complete their current terms. The opinion states the request was received on 24 May 2016. This is a different opinion and a different draft from CON/2016/52 of 28 October 2016, which the map already holds for Croatia.
records.quote: are not in line with the principle of central bank independence referred to in Article 130 of the Treaty
records.source_title: Opinion of the European Central Bank of 15 June 2016 on amendments to the Law on Hrvatska Narodna Banka (CON/2016/33)

records.summary: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe Amendment Act, Act 1 of 2010, made two of the Bank's functions under section 6(1) of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe Act subject to any written directions given to it by the Minister, inserted a provision letting the Minister direct in writing that the Bank establish additional reserves, required the Board to send its minutes to the Minister within seven days of each meeting, and seated a Ministry of Finance employee on both the Board and a newly inserted Audit and Oversight Committee.
records.detail: Read in the consolidated Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe Act [Chapter 22:15] on ZimLII, in the consolidation stated as current to 31 December 2021, whose history notes mark each amended provision; the amendments described here are the ones that consolidation attributes to Act 1 of 2010 at sections 6(1)(h) and (k), 49(5), 28(4)-(5), 21(2) and 29A. The Act is shown as in force in that consolidation, with later amendments listed up to the Finance Act 2021. The consolidation gives the amending instrument only as Act 1 of 2010 and states no promulgation day, so the date field carries the year only. The map's existing Zimbabwe record is the 2009 public clash between the finance minister and the governor; this is the enacted legislation, a separate instrument, and the two are part of the same period of conflict.
records.source_title: Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe Act [Chapter 22:15], consolidation to 31 December 2021 (ZimLII)

records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
records.summary: Section 52 of the Reserve Bank of Fiji Act, headed 'Policy directives', provides that the Minister may, after consultation with the Board, issue to the Reserve Bank such written directives of a general nature as may be necessary to give effect to the economic policies of the Government, and that the Reserve Bank shall comply with them. Section 51(5) separately lets the Minister direct the Bank to permit temporary increases in its lending to Government up to 40 per cent of average annual ordinary revenue.
records.detail: Read in the text of the Act published by the Reserve Bank of Fiji itself (167,051-byte PDF on rbf.gov.fj, uploaded under a 2020 path, extracted in full to 54,778 characters). The document's own running head is 'Cap.210 Rev.1985', so the version the bank publishes is the revised edition of 1985 and consolidates nothing later; the date field carries 1983, the year of the principal Act as the Act is cited, and the wording quoted is from that revised edition as the central bank currently publishes it. Not checked against post-1985 amending Acts, which are on PacLII and were not opened. Distinct from the 2009 dismissal of Governor Savenaca Narube, which the map already holds for Fiji.
records.quote: The Minister may, after consultation with the Board, issue to the Reserve Bank such written directives of a general nature
records.source_title: Reserve Bank of Fiji Act, Cap. 210 (Rev. 1985), s 52 (Reserve Bank of Fiji)

records.kind: the bank objects in writing to a government bill
records.summary: In a letter of 27 June 2023 to Prime Minister Binyamin Netanyahu, Bank of Israel Governor Amir Yaron expressed his vehement opposition to a bill, approved two days earlier by the Ministerial Committee on Legislation, that would require banks to pay interest on customers' current account balances at a minimum rate set by the Governor in consultation with the Advisory Committee and subject to approval by the Minister of Finance, and asked the Prime Minister to have the proposal removed from the agenda immediately.
records.detail: Read in the letter itself, published as a PDF on the Bank of Israel's own site. Yaron wrote that making the Governor set a minimum current-account interest rate subject to the Finance Minister's approval was a serious blow to the independence of the Bank of Israel and its ability to conduct monetary policy, that it grants the Minister of Finance authority to actively influence the interest rate in the economy, and that the undermining of independence inherent in the proposed law crosses a significant red line. The letter states the Ministerial Committee on Legislation chaired by the Minister of Justice approved the proposal on 25 June 2023 and that it was scheduled for a preliminary reading vote on Wednesday 28 June 2023; copies went to the Minister of Finance, Bezalel Smotrich, among others. Distinct from the September 2025 public-pressure record the map holds for Israel.
records.quote: a serious blow to the independence of the Bank of Israel and its ability to conduct monetary policy
records.source_title: Letter from Governor Amir Yaron to Prime Minister Binyamin Netanyahu on the Proposed Banking (Service to the Customer) (Interest on Positive Balances Amendment) Law, 5783-2023 (Bank of Israel)

records.kind: governing parties agree to replace the bank's board
records.summary: Reporting from Montevideo in July 2002, Pagina/12 wrote that at a political summit the leaders of the governing Colorado and Blanco parties decided to replace the three directors of the Banco Central del Uruguay, after criticism of the conduct of the central bank's president, Cesar Rodriguez Batlle, over the timing of the intervention in Banco Montevideo and Caja Obrera; President Jorge Batlle had proposed Carlos Steneri as the next central bank president.
records.detail: Read in the Pagina/12 article of Tuesday 23 July 2002, which carries the sentence 'se decidio la sustitucion de los tres directores del Banco Central' and places that decision on 'el viernes', the Friday before publication, that is 19 July 2002 - the day is derived from the publication date and is not printed on the page, so the date field carries the month only. The article also reports that the Blanco director Rosario Medero had already resigned the previous week. The article does not state that Rodriguez Batlle had been removed by the date of publication, so this record is the political decision to replace the board, not a completed dismissal. Uruguay's existing record on this row is the 1967 constitutional arrangement, so this is the country's first episode on the row.
records.source_title: Pagina/12, 23 July 2002 (El Mundo) - report on the replacement of the Banco Central del Uruguay's directors

records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the head of state appoint and remove the bank's governor
records.summary: Under the Central Bank and Banking Sector Law No. 194 of 2020, the Central Bank of Egypt reports to the President of the Republic while enjoying technical, financial and administrative independence; the Governor is appointed by presidential decree following approval by a majority of the House of Representatives for a renewable four-year term, holds the rank equivalent to Deputy Prime Minister, and may be dismissed by presidential decree on the Board's recommendation after being allowed to present a defence.
records.detail: Read in an English translation of the law published as a PDF by Andersen Egypt (874,971 bytes, extracted to 140,776 characters): Article 2 for reporting to the President, Article 17 for appointment and remuneration by presidential decree, Article 18 for the deputies, and Article 24 for dismissal grounds, which are loss of required qualifications, incapacity for health reasons, serious breach of duty and unexcused absence from three consecutive or five non-consecutive Board meetings in a year. The source is a professional law-firm translation rather than the Official Gazette, which is why this is marked a weak source; the Arabic original was not opened. Distinct from the 2015 public-pressure record and the uncounted 2022 record the map holds for Egypt.
records.source_title: Central Bank and Banking Sector Law No. 194 of 2020, English translation (Andersen Egypt)

blanks.read: KAZ: a real candidate failed the row's rules. Tengrinews (en.tengrinews.kz, 17 January 2025, 'National Bank responded to the President's criticism') was read in full: the criticism President Tokayev made in his Ana tili interview of 3 January 2025 was of the country's economic bloc and of insufficient growth, and the article states he did not name the National Bank. The only link to the bank is Governor Timur Suleimenov's own reading of the remarks at a National Bank briefing as an assessment of a bloc that includes the National Bank - reported speech by the bank's own head, which is not the state acting on the bank. Nothing filed. The 2015 dismissal of Kairat Kelimbetov remains the country's only record on this row. Vein still open: Akorda's own published addresses and the National Bank's annual report to the President were not opened.

MLI: searched for a national event after the March 2012 coup to replace the BCEAO union record the map expands into Mali. The search returned only ECOWAS/BCEAO measures against the Malian state's own accounts and transactions (BCEAO press release on the extraordinary Council of Ministers meeting, and notei042012.pdf on bceao.int, neither opened). That shape is explicitly refused on this row - an act on the state's money held at the union bank, where the bank is custodian and not subject - so the route was closed without spending a fetch on it. A national Malian organ acting on the BCEAO's Bamako agency was not found by this search. Not converted.

Its three Israeli case records (Frenkel 2002, banking supervision 2009, market operations 2008-2012) are findings about the bank's own officials and none concerns the June 2023 interest-on-balances bill, so the new record is not that episode under another description.

leads_not_opened: ECB opinions reached through national central banks' own sites remain the best repeatable vein on this row. hnb.hr publishes the opinions on Croatian drafts as PDFs under /documents/, and CON/2016/33 found this round was sitting one link from the page a search returns for the opinion the map already held. The same shape should be tried for every EU and candidate-country member whose only record is one ECB opinion.

Croatia has at least one further opinion not opened: the search returned lagen.nu guidance pages for CON/2015/32 (Swiss franc loan conversion), CON/2019/25 and CON/2020/10. lagen.nu is robots-disallowed; the route is hnb.hr's own opinion pages. CON/2015/32 was judged unpromising on this row because its subject is commercial banks rather than the HNB.

Australia: the Senate Economics Legislation Committee report on the Treasury Laws Amendment (Reserve Bank Reforms) Bill 2024 is published on aph.gov.au, including a Coalition senators' dissenting report. Parliament's own evidence on the restructuring of the RBA board is a candidate for a second Australian episode, but needs the consent test applied carefully, since the RBA publicly supported parts of the review.

Israel: the Bank of Israel publishes its written positions on bills under boi.org.il/media/. Other letters in that series are likely further records of the same family, and the Knesset's own committee protocols would carry the tabling and vote dates the letter only forecasts.

Philippines: the Senate's issuances-library and legacy hosts both appeared in search results for RA 11954; the legacy.senate.gov.ph PDFs of the committee report would carry the BSP's own position on the dividend diversion, which this record deliberately does not assert.

Zimbabwe: parlzim.gov.zw returned a page in the search for the 2009-2010 RBZ Amendment Bill and was not opened. Parliament's own debate on that Bill would carry the grounds, and ZimLII also lists a Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe Amendment Act 1 of 2017 that nothing on the map uses.

Fiji: PacLII hosts a consolidation of the Reserve Bank of Fiji Act (pacliirms.paclii.org/fj/legis/consol_act/rbofa179) and the 1995 amendment act. Opening it would date section 52 in its current form and confirm the post-1985 amendments the central bank's own published text does not carry.
Egypt: the Arabic original of Law 194 of 2020 in al-Jarida al-Rasmiyya would replace the law-firm translation this record rests on and remove the weak-source flag.
